Subject: [Incident] US-WEST1 throughput signal impacting hosted inference - OrchidAI

Hi Sam,

Quick heads-up: our monitoring flagged an elevated throughput signal in the US-WEST1 hosted inference fleet starting ~08:05 PST that is increasing p95 response times for generation endpoints for a subset of customers (incident INC-3819 on our status page). You may see longer tails or intermittent 503/429s on batch jobs.

What we know so far:
- Impact window: started ~08:05 PST, ongoing
- Affected surface: hosted generation endpoints in us-west1 (routing may fall back to other regions for some requests)
- Observable to you: elevated latency on multi-input batch jobs and occasional request retries

Mitigation in progress:
- We have an SRE bridge open and are rolling a conservative KV-cache eviction tuning change to reduce contention.
- Temporary routing policy to route long-context requests to a dedicated pool where possible (may increase latency for very large requests).

Action for you:
- Please share any specific job IDs or example request timestamps so we can correlate.
- If this is blocking critical pipelines we can discuss escalating to dedicated routing for your account.

I attached an ops snapshot with current queue metrics. I will update as soon as we have an ETA. We’re treating this as high priority.

Best,

Hi all — quick technical update from SRE. We investigated the fleet traces and KV-cache telemetry. Initial root cause hypothesis: a short spike of concurrent long-context requests triggered aggressive KV-cache evictions which caused cache thrash on a subset of inference hosts. That increased token-servicing overhead and led to a higher p95 and a small set of transient 5xx responses during rehydration.

What we did:
- Deployed a conservative eviction-threshold rollback to reduce thrash (rolling restart of ~20% of hosts ongoing).
- Tuned the batching window for generation paths that overlap with long-context workloads.
- Enabled an emergency prefix-KV warmup on recently evicted keys to reduce cold misses.

Expected impact:
- We expect p95 to return within ~90 minutes after the rollout completes (ETA ~14:15 PST).
- No evidence of silent data loss; requests that returned 5xx were not persisted as successful — customers should see retries/failures but not incorrect silent successes.

We’ve attached an eviction graph and a short excerpt of the trace. I will circle back with the full postmortem and remediation plan once validated.

Evelyn
SRE Manager, Redwood Inference

Subject: Incident update: INC-3819 resolved (US-WEST1 throughput signal)

Hi Sam — following up to confirm that incident INC-3819 has been resolved as of 10:30 PST on 2026-02-19. The conservative eviction thresholds and batching adjustments completed overnight; p95 metrics have returned to normal and we are not seeing continued 5xx patterns for the affected endpoints.

Summary:
- Root cause: cache eviction thrash triggered by a spike in concurrent long-context requests on a subset of hosts
- Impact: elevated p95 and transient 5xx (observable in your batch job logs)
- Customer-facing effect: some batch jobs saw retries/failures; no silent data loss confirmed
- Remediation: rollback of aggressive eviction policy, batching window tweak, and emergency warmup rollout

Next steps:
- We will publish a detailed postmortem with timeline and permanent mitigations (INC-3819 postmortem link below) by EOD Friday.
- If you’d like, we can open a separate ticket to discuss routing your critical batches to a dedicated pool for greater isolation.

Status links:
- Public incident page: https://status.redwoodinference.com/incidents/INC-3819
- Internal postmortem: https://internal.redwoodinference.com/incidents/INC-3819/postmortem

Thanks again for the quick context and the job IDs — that helped us correlate traces faster. I’ll keep the ticket open until we publish the postmortem.

Best,
